items.title: Influencers pushed mercury-laced cream; a 17-year-old Keralam girl paid with her kidneys
items.summary: A 17-year-old girl in Malappuram is recovering from a serious kidney disorder after using Ftune, a fairness cream promoted by multiple Instagram influencers. Doctors at a private hospital, who tested the product found that the cream contained 12,500 parts per million (1.25 per cent) of mercury, more than 12,000 times the 1 ppm limit set for most cosmetics in India. Mercury is a toxic heavy metal, and decades of research have warned against its use in cosmetics. The usage of Skin Lightening Products (SLPs) have often been linked to prejudice against people with darker skin by centuries of colonialism, white supremacy and classism, and a multi-crore fairness industry thrives on it. The plight of the teenager has now prompted the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights to register a suo motu case. The teenager developed a severe kidney disorder, membranous nephropathy, in which immune deposits thicken the filtering walls of the kidneys, caused by mercury poisoning linked to the cream. The case came to light after the girl sought medical treatment at a private hospital in Malappuram after she experienced leg and face swelling, difficulty walking and climbing stairs, fainting, and a sharp drop in blood pressure. According to the doctor, Gouri S, a nephrologist at Aster MIMS Mother Hospital in Malappuram who treated the girl, tests on the cream detected 12,500 parts per million (ppm) (1.25%) of mercury, far above the permissible limit of less than 1 ppm. “Membranous nephropathy is a serious kidney disease that can become very dangerous if left untreated, potentially leading to several other complications. It is very clear that the mercury-containing cream was responsible for causing these health problems in this girl,” the doctor told the media. “They are selling this product, Ftune, by claiming that it will remove pimples, dark spots and pigmentation. They advertise it through Instagram, and they also provide a WhatsApp contact number through which we can purchase the product,” the girl told the media about how she ordered the cream. When the cream gave a visible result, she purchased it again and used it for nearly a year. Later, she developed health issues, which were later found to be membranous nephropathy. “Whenever I urinate, my blood pressure suddenly drops, causing me to feel dizzy and faint.
